correctness.rationale: For c<d equal squarefree factorial parts require a square consecutive product, hence d=c+1=t² by Erdős--Selfridge. Thus consecutive-largest representation multiplicity is 0,1,2, with duplicated class b_t=s((t²)!). Published exponential growth s(m!)≥exp(delta m) yields b_t≥exp(delta t²), absolute convergence of K and O(sqrt(log(2X))) doubled-family counting error. Yudin Section 3.2 yields C0 sqrt X+O(log X) distinct consecutive-largest endpoints. Yudin Theorem 3.1 plus eq. (3.2) give O_eps(X^(2/5+eps)) nonconsecutive triples with their multiplicities by counting O(X^(2eta)) parameters for each exceptional endpoint. The exact finite parity-signature program verifies examples through 260 but is not used to prove the infinite assertions.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Published ingredients imply a short deduction, which this finding makes explicit and sharp: squarefree-kernel duplicates contribute a new positive leading constant K to the count of triples; E(X) and (3.2) bound the remaining weighted triples by O_eps(X^(2/5+eps)). originality.rationale: The correction counts representations rather than endpoints. Tao explicitly stated the square-index repetition, but subsequently conjectured the distinct-endpoint coefficient for all ordered triples. Yudin proves a distinct-endpoint asymptotic, not the multiplicity-corrected triple count; the argument here combines that theorem with an exact duplicate-series asymptotic and a multiplicity-weighted exceptional bound. Relevant primary full-text passages and published result catalog searches did not identify the corrected coefficient. Residual possibility of a previously noted implicit correction is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Earlier uncatalogued commentary may already note the short logical correction to Tao Remark 1.11.
Erdős--Selfridge original 1975 article was not directly read; its standard theorem is quoted in two inspected primary sources.
Asymptotic depends on published nonconsecutive-endpoint analytic estimates; these were applied with their stated quantifiers, not independently reproved.
Finite checks do not certify a numerical high-precision limit of K.

value.rationale: Corrects an explicit conjectural coefficient for a significant 2026 factorial-square enumeration problem by distinguishing numbers that admit a triple from distinct triples. Identifies a strictly positive new series K in the leading term, sharp restricted collision classification and sparse multiplicity law. Derives a nonzero conditional fraction of double representations among three-factorable nonsquare endpoints. No claim of new proof of the cited classical theorem, and no unsupported applications are asserted.
